Question!

2

What is to be observed in reading & passing one's judgment on poets?

3

Is only the versification, the style & grammatical construction to be minded? So far the grammarian takes only notice and is contented. But, the more material things to be observed are the table or poet's invention; the matter or action; the formal disposition or narration; the style & expression; and particularly, the manners or characters of the personages introduced and the moral sentiments of the poet.

4

A critique goes farther to ensure the poet's maximes & knowledge in divinity, law, history, chronology, philosophy & mathematicks; these being sciences ancillary to a poet. Few poets may be found that can stand the test, even–Virgil himself and all others before him & since having erred in one point or other.
